primary.title: Noel Tata says Tata Sons can't bypass rules for IPO
primary.description: Mumbai: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has said he’s against a proposed extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of Tata Sons, arguing that it can’t pursue a public offering without first converting itself into a public company and amending its Articles of Association. He has also challenged the validity of a September 17 board resolution on N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman, saying it did not secure the affirmative vote required under the company’s Articles.In a November 25 letter to company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay that ET has seen, Noel Tata also objected to the agenda for the November 30 board meeting, demanding that directors first consider his earlier notices on the Reserve Bank of India’s regulatory directions, the proposed restructuring of Tata Sons and disclosures relating to transactions involving group entities. This latest communication comes amid the ongoing turmoil over control of the Tata group with Noel Tata pitted against other directors of the holding company.136172071Also read: Tata Sons postpones board meeting to November 30On the proposed EGM, Noel said the board had unanimously resolved on March 21, 2024, that Tata Sons would repay its debt, stop accessing public funds and seek surrender of its RBI registration. “That resolution has not been rescinded, and the board has not decided to depart from it,” he wrote.He questioned the rationale for considering a public offer before the board had examined the September 28 proposal from Tata Trusts to reorganise the company, which he said was intended to address regulatory compliance. He also cautioned against making commitments to the RBI on listing without board approval, saying: “No undertaking, timetable or other commitment as to listing can be given to the Reserve Bank of India without a decision of the board.”Noel Tata further argued that any proposal to alter the Articles of Association or issue shares required an affirmative vote under Article 121. The board could not bypass this requirement by convening a general meeting, he said.On Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, Noel Tata said the September 17 resolution was invalid as it had not secured the affirmative vote required under Article 121 and Article 118. “A resolution of the board cannot take the place of either, and the company should not ask its members to act upon that resolution,” he wrote.He also questioned the proposed EGM to consider Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman, arguing that his reappointment as a director was already pending before shareholders. The annual general meeting was adjourned on August 18 due to lack of quorum, with the deadline extended to December 31. Until shareholders vote, it remains unclear whether Chandrasekaran will continue as a director, he said.Noel Tata also said a director whose reappointment or appointment terms were under consideration should not participate in the discussion or vote. “This applies to Mr Chandrasekaran on every item which concerns his reappointment or the terms of his appointment,” he wrote.Separately, Noel Tata said three matters he had formally raised under Article 121B had been placed sixth on the November 30 agenda, after discussions on RBI correspondence and the proposed EGM. He said the provision required these matters to be considered first and asked the company to revise the agenda.The matters include disclosures relating to dealings between TVS Motor Co. and Hanno One Warehousing, the constitution of a selection committee under Article 118 and the RBI’s September 11 letter, alongside the Tata Trusts restructuring proposal. The TVS-Hanno matter relates to allegations of conflict of interest that involve Tata Sons board member Venu Srinivasan and Chandrasekaran. The TVS chairman emeritus had backed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment at the September 17 meeting.Also read: Chandrasekaran to push Tata Sons IPO plan at board meet, company valued at up to Rs 18 lakh croreNoel Tata also sought a detailed management presentation on the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s proposal regarding the monetisation of its stake in Tata Sons, including valuation, capital reduction structure, timeline and key terms, as well as the legal advice obtained by the company.He questioned how a quorum would be ensured at the proposed EGM, given that the AGM had been adjourned for lack of quorum. He sought the draft EGM notice, explanatory statement and legal advice, as well as confirmation on whether Tata Trusts, which together hold about two-thirds of Tata Sons’ equity, had been consulted.He asked for the November 30 board meeting to be recorded in full in audio and video, with the recording preserved and made available to directors on request. He also sought circulation of his letter and November 22 email to all directors and a response by November 26.The letter was copied to all directors of Tata Sons. Noel said his objections should not be construed as acceptance of the validity of the September 17 resolution or any item on the November 30 agenda and reserved all his rights and remedies.

This latest communication comes amid the ongoing turmoil over control of the Tata group with Noel Tata pitted against other directors of the holding company.136172071Also read: Tata Sons postpones board meeting to November 30On the proposed EGM, Noel said the board had unanimously resolved on March 21, 2024, that Tata Sons would repay its debt, stop accessing public funds and seek surrender of its RBI registration. “That resolution has not been rescinded, and the board has not decided to depart from it,” he wrote.He questioned the rationale for considering a public offer before the board had examined the September 28 proposal from Tata Trusts to reorganise the company, which he said was intended to address regulatory compliance. He also cautioned against making commitments to the RBI on listing without board approval, saying: “No undertaking, timetable or other commitment as to listing can be given to the Reserve Bank of India without a decision of the board.”Noel Tata further argued that any proposal to alter the Articles of Association or issue shares required an affirmative vote under Article 121. The board could not bypass this requirement by convening a general meeting, he said.On Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, Noel Tata said the September 17 resolution was invalid as it had not secured the affirmative vote required under Article 121 and Article 118. “A resolution of the board cannot take the place of either, and the company should not ask its members to act upon that resolution,” he wrote.He also questioned the proposed EGM to consider Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman, arguing that his reappointment as a director was already pending before shareholders. The annual general meeting was adjourned on August 18 due to lack of quorum, with the deadline extended to December 31. Until shareholders vote, it remains unclear whether Chandrasekaran will continue as a director, he said.Noel Tata also said a director whose reappointment or appointment terms were under consideration should not participate in the discussion or vote. “This applies to Mr Chandrasekaran on every item which concerns his reappointment or the terms of his appointment,” he wrote.Separately, Noel Tata said three matters he had formally raised under Article 121B had been placed sixth on the November 30 agenda, after discussions on RBI correspondence and the proposed EGM. He said the provision required these matters to be considered first and asked the company to revise the agenda.The matters include disclosures relating to dealings between TVS Motor Co. and Hanno One Warehousing, the constitution of a selection committee under Article 118 and the RBI’s September 11 letter, alongside the Tata Trusts restructuring proposal. The TVS-Hanno matter relates to allegations of conflict of interest that involve Tata Sons board member Venu Srinivasan and Chandrasekaran. The TVS chairman emeritus had backed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment at the September 17 meeting.Also read: Chandrasekaran to push Tata Sons IPO plan at board meet, company valued at up to Rs 18 lakh croreNoel Tata also sought a detailed management presentation on the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s proposal regarding the monetisation of its stake in Tata Sons, including valuation, capital reduction structure, timeline and key terms, as well as the legal advice obtained by the company.He questioned how a quorum would be ensured at the proposed EGM, given that the AGM had been adjourned for lack of quorum. He sought the draft EGM notice, explanatory statement and legal advice, as well as confirmation on whether Tata Trusts, which together hold about two-thirds of Tata Sons’ equity, had been consulted.He asked for the November 30 board meeting to be recorded in full in audio and video, with the recording preserved and made available to directors on request. He also sought circulation of his letter and November 22 email to all directors and a response by November 26.The letter was copied to all directors of Tata Sons. Noel said his objections should not be construed as acceptance of the validity of the September 17 resolution or any item on the November 30 agenda and reserved all his rights and remedies.
